schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT A1.FIRST_LOGIN AS INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN (A1.FIRST_LOGIN + 1) = A2.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/ COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID)), 2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS A1 JOIN ACTIVITY AS A2 ON A1.PLAYER_ID = A2.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY A1.FIRST_LOGIN
q2: SELECT INSTALL_DT, COUNT(D1.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN D2.PLAYER_ID THEN D2.PLAYER_ID ELSE NULL END)/CAST(COUNT(D1.PLAYER_ID) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS INSTALL_DT FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY 1) D1 LEFT JOIN ACTIVITY D2 ON D1.PLAYER_ID = D2.PLAYER_ID AND D1.INSTALL_DT + 1 = D2.EVENT_DATE GROUP BY 1

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 uses a JOIN to calculate the day1_retention, while Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN and a CASE statement. This difference can lead to different results if there are NULL values in the data.
counterexample_dsp: The difference in results can be observed when there are NULL values in the data. Q1 will not count NULL values in the day1_retention calculation, while Q2 will count NULL values as 0.
